title: Changes to the Standard: Sharing Bandwidth
markdown:
## Changes in the Standard

The 10-Mbps Standard Ethernet went through several changes before
moving to higher data rates. These changes opened the road to
Ethernet's evolution toward compatibility with other high-data-rate
LANs.

{{viz:0}}

Two side-by-side Rate-vs-Time charts, both with a dashed reference line
at 5 Mbps under a 10 Mbps axis ceiling:

- **(a) First station** — pale pink bars, each labeled "One frame",
  repeating over time.
- **(b) Second station** — darker magenta/pink bars, each also labeled
  "One frame", repeating over time in the same pattern.

Both stations' frames occupy the same rate/time pattern, illustrating
that when stations share a 10 Mbps link, each effectively gets an
average around 5 Mbps.
